exposure: cord polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) concentrations (n-3 PUFA, n-6:n-3 ratio)
outcome: cord cytokine concentrations (IFN-g, IL-1b, IL-2, IL-12p70, TNF-a, IL-4, IL-10, IL-13, IL-6, IL-8)
cohort: Participants were from the Seychelles Child Development Study (SCDS) Nutrition Cohort 2 (NC2), a large birth cohort from a high fish-eating population (n = 878).
finding: Methylmercury exposure from fish consumption does not appear to impact markers of inflammation in cord blood, while increased total n-3 PUFA is significantly associated with lower IL-10 and total Th2 cytokines.
